title: Washington WSDOT pipe trench, bedding and backfill numbers (Section 7-08)
topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
text: Washington (WSDOT Standard Specifications M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-08, general pipe installation). Trench: remove ledge rock, boulders and stones to give at least 6 inches clearance under all parts of the pipe; keep the toe of the spoil pile at least 2 feet from the trench edge; shoring is called for in trenches 4 feet or deeper that don't meet the open-pit rules of 3-07.3(3)B (7-08.3(1)A). Bedding: compact to 90 percent of maximum density, in lifts no more than 6 inches thick along the sides of the pipe; fix line and grade by scraping or filling under the barrel, never by blocking or wedging (7-08.3(1)C). Backfill (7-08.3(3)): pipe zone compacted to 90 percent, no rocks or lumps over 3 inches; under existing pavement or roadways 6-inch layers at 95 percent; in non-traffic areas 6-inch layers at 85 percent. No tractors or heavy equipment over the pipe until backfill is 3 feet above the top of the pipe. Laying tolerance: invert within plus or minus 0.03 foot at the time of backfill, and never a reverse slope (7-08.3(2)B). Your contract's special provisions and the city's own amendments can change these numbers.
source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Washington WSDOT storm sewer tests (Section 7-04)
topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-04.3(1), storm sewers). Exfiltration test: leakage no more than 1 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet, with at least 6 feet of water above the crown; the allowance rises 10 percent for each extra 2 feet of head, and pressure at the low-end invert is capped at 16 feet of water (7-04.3(1)B). Infiltration test: no more than 0.8 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet (7-04.3(1)C). Low-pressure air test: the pressure-drop time must be at least the table time, for example 80 seconds for 100 feet of 12-inch pipe; pipe that does not pass air (plastic, lined) needs four times the table time; pipe over 30 inches is tested joint by joint under ASTM C1103 (7-04.3(1)E and F). Sanitary sewers are stricter: see Section 7-17.
source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Washington WSDOT sanitary sewer tests: air, water, mandrel, TV (Section 7-17)
topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-17.3(2), sanitary sewers). Clean and test within 15 working days after backfilling. Exfiltration: no more than 0.28 gallon per hour per inch of diameter per 100 feet, with 6 feet of head over the crown at the upper end (or over groundwater if higher), test length no more than 700 feet, no more than 16 feet of head at the low invert (7-17.3(2)B). Infiltration: 0.16 gallon per hour per inch per 100 feet when groundwater head is 2 feet or less (7-17.3(2)C). Add 0.2 gallon per hour per foot of head for each manhole in the test section (D). Low-pressure air test for pipe 30 inches and smaller: pump to 4 psig, wait at least 2 minutes, then time the drop from 3.5 to 2.5 psig; the time comes from K = 0.0111 x d squared x L and C = 0.0003918 x d x L (E); pipe that does not pass air needs four times that time (F); over 30 inches test each joint under ASTM C1103. Deflection test for thermoplastic pipe: not less than 30 days after trench backfill and compaction are complete, with a mandrel that has an odd number of legs (9 or more) and is 95 percent of the pipe's base inside diameter (G). The Engineer can require TV inspection (H).
source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Washington WSDOT water main: cover, backfill, pressure test, disinfection (Section 7-09)
topic: Spec books: water main installation, pressure test and disinfection
text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition, Section 7-09, water mains). Minimum cover 36 inches over the top of the pipe; at least 1 foot over valve operating nuts. Trench width up to 1 foot above the pipe: no more than 30 inches or 1.5 times the pipe outside diameter plus 18 inches, whichever is greater. Bedding compacted to 95 percent of maximum density (7-09.3(9)); backfill to at least 95 percent, in layers of 6 inches loose or less under paved areas (7-09.3(11)). Hydrostatic test (7-09.3(23)): 150 psi above operating pressure and never less than 225 psi; sections normally no longer than 1,500 feet; pump up, stop for 15 minutes, pump back to test pressure; allowable leakage L = S x D x square root of P / 266,400 (L gallons per hour, S feet of pipe, D inches, P psi). Disinfection (7-09.3(24)): at least 50 mg/L chlorine to start, hold at least 24 hours, at least 25 mg/L left after 24 hours; flush at 2.5 feet per second or more; dechlorinate the flush water to 0.1 ppm or less and pH 6.5 to 8.5. Services 2 inch and smaller need 3 feet of cover (7-15); hydrants need a 3-foot clear radius and the sidewalk flange 2 inches above finished grade (7-14).
source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Washington WSDOT manholes, catch basins, side sewers and cleanouts (Sections 7-05, 7-18, 7-19)
topic: Spec books: manholes, inlets and catch basins
text: Washington (WSDOT M 41-10, 2027 edition). Manholes, inlets and catch basins (7-05): dig to leave 1 foot clear between the structure and the bank; ladder rungs at 12 inches; rigid pipe entering a sanitary manhole needs a flexible joint within 1.5 pipe diameters or 18 inches of the wall, whichever is greater; manholes over 10 feet are paid per extra foot; an abandoned manhole is broken down to at least 4 feet below the new surface and filled with sand compacted to 90 percent. Side sewers (7-18): joint deflection never more than 2 inches per foot, use 1/8 bends for bigger turns; a 6-inch test tee goes where the side sewer crosses the right-of-way line; mark the end with a 2x4 stake 4 feet long buried 3 feet. Cleanouts (7-19): at each total 90 degrees of change in grade or alignment, never more than 100 feet apart, same size as the side sewer.
source: WSDOT Standard Specifications for Road, Bridge, and Municipal Construction, M 41-10, 2027 edition, Division 7 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Texas TxDOT pipe excavation, bedding and backfill (Items 400, 401, 402)
topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications). Item 400, Excavation and Backfill for Structures: pipe gets Class C bedding unless the plans show something else; for precast concrete pipe the ASTM C1479 beddings are allowed (400.3.2). Pipe backfill goes in uniform layers no more than 8 inches deep (loose), each lift compacted mechanically, with the haunches thoroughly compacted (400.3.3.3); each layer must meet the density required for the roadbed (400.3.3.1; the percent comes from the embankment item and the plans, not Item 400). Cement-stabilized backfill: at least 7 percent cement by dry weight of aggregate, placed and compacted within 2 hours of mixing (400.3.3.4). Flowable backfill (Item 401, Table 2): excavatable mix 80 to 200 psi at 28 days; non-excavatable over 200 psi. Trench protection (Item 402): furnish and place excavation protection for trenches 5 feet or greater in depth, following OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P.
source: TxDOT Standard Specifications for Construction and Maintenance of Highways, Streets, and Bridges, 2024, Items 400, 401, 402 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Texas TxDOT concrete pipe, metal pipe and box culverts (Items 460, 462, 464)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications). Item 464, Reinforced Concrete Pipe: circular pipe Classes I through V (D-loads 800 to 3,000); joints may be mortar, cold-applied asphalt joint compound, rubber gaskets (ASTM C1619 Class A or C) or preformed flexible sealant (ASTM C990); arch and elliptical pipe need at least 1 foot of cover; do not run heavy earth-moving equipment over the pipe until at least 4 feet of compacted fill is in place unless the plans or the Engineer allow it in writing (464.3.1). Item 460, Corrugated Metal Pipe: lay from the outlet end with laps pointing upstream; same 4-foot rule for heavy earth-moving equipment (460.3.2); bell-and-spigot gaskets to ASTM F477 with at least a 6-inch stab depth. Item 462, Concrete Box Culverts: no more than four lifting holes per precast section, each 3 inches or smaller; boxes with joints that are not mortar can be backfilled right away. Jacking, boring or tunneling any of these is under Item 476.
source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, 2024, Items 460, 462, 464 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Texas TxDOT thermoplastic pipe (HDPE, PP, PVC): backfill, mandrel and deflection limits (Item 468)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications, Item 468, Thermoplastic Pipe). Bedding at least 4 inches thick, 6 inches where large rocks are present (468.3). Granular backfill goes in uniform loose layers about 6 inches deep up to 12 inches above the pipe; within 12 inches of the pipe use only hand-operated tampers; with flowable backfill the trench is pipe outside diameter plus 12 inches, the fill is carried at least 12 inches above the pipe, and you wait 24 hours before backfilling the rest (468.3.11). Stop backfilling if measured deflection passes 5 percent. No heavy earth-moving equipment over the pipe until at least 4 feet of compacted fill is in place (468.3.12). Final inspection (468.4.1): at least 30 days after backfill is complete, pull a mandrel sized at 95 percent of the pipe diameter through the whole length; if it will not pass, a 92.5 percent mandrel is tried and a remote camera is used to look at joints, cracks, deflection and ponding. Pipe deflected more than 7.5 percent of nominal diameter must be fixed or replaced (468.4.2). Joints: the bell must overlap at least two corrugations of the spigot.
source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, 2024, Item 468 Thermoplastic Pipe (read 2026-11-20)

title: Texas TxDOT jacking, boring and tunneling pipe; manholes and inlets (Items 476, 465, 479)
topic: Spec books: jacking, boring and tunneling
text: Texas (TxDOT 2024 Standard Specifications). Item 476, Jacking, Boring, or Tunneling Pipe or Box: line and grade may not vary more than 1 inch in 10 feet; over-excavation no more than 2 inches at the top and sides, and anything over 1 inch is pressure grouted; do not excavate more than 2 feet ahead of the pipe; keep jacking going without interruption so the pipe does not set up; parallel jacked or tunneled lines need at least 3 feet clear between them; use plywood cushions between pipe ends, 1/2 inch minimum for pipe 30 inches and smaller and 3/4 inch for larger pipe and boxes; boring starts with a 2-inch pilot hole; keep a 3:1 slope from the edge of pavement on the shaft side. Item 465, Junction Boxes, Manholes, and Inlets: structures with rubber boots, gaskets or preformed sealant joints can be backfilled right away; place and compact backfill so the structure does not move. Item 479, adjusting manholes and inlets: flexible extension rings no taller than 3 inches; when capping, remove the structure to at least 1 foot below subgrade. Item 471 castings are load tested at 40,000 lb on a 9 by 9 inch block for 1 minute.
source: TxDOT Standard Specifications, 2024, Items 465, 471, 476, 479 (read 2026-11-20)

title: California Caltrans structure backfill and compaction numbers (Sections 19-3, 19-5)
topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
text: California (Caltrans 2025 Standard Specifications, Section 19 Earthwork). Structure backfill, which is what goes around culverts and drainage structures: layers no more than 0.67 foot (8 inches) thick before compacting; relative compaction at least 95 percent; at least 90 percent is allowed at overside drains, headwalls, endwalls, culvert wingwalls and similar spots with nothing under pavement (19-3.03E(1)). Ponding and jetting is allowed only where the backfill drains freely and the foundation will not soften, in layers up to 4 feet, never in the top 4 feet below finished grade, and with vibratory compaction added. Slurry cement backfill: at least 188 lb of cement per cubic yard, placed within 1 hour of mixing, and nothing placed over it for at least 4 hours (19-3.02E, 19-3.03F). Soil cement bedding: at least 282 lb of cement per cubic yard and an 8-hour wait (19-3.02F(3), 19-3.03H). Embankment (19-5): 95 percent for 0.5 foot below the grading plane and 2.5 feet below finished grade under the traveled way plus 3 feet each side; 90 percent elsewhere. Caltrans 'relative compaction' is by California Test 216/231, not Proctor.
source: Caltrans Standard Specifications, 2025, Sections 19-3 and 19-5 (read 2026-11-20)

title: California Caltrans drainage pipe joints and leak tests (Section 61)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: California (Caltrans 2025 Standard Specifications, Section 61, Drainage Facilities, general). Pipe materials have their own sections: plastic pipe Section 64, concrete pipe Section 65, corrugated metal pipe Section 66. Watertight joints are proven by holding a 10-foot head of water above the pipe crown for 10 minutes (61-2.01D(2)(b)). Field leak testing is done on culverts and drainage structures only where the plans show it (61-2.01D(3)(a)); the low-pressure air test is not used on drainage pipe over 30 inches (61-2.01D(3)(c)). Concrete backfill in pipe trenches is consolidated with high-frequency internal vibrators, and with rapid-strength concrete nothing goes on top until it reaches 500 psi (61-5.03). For plastic pipe in saturated clay, unsuitable material is removed at least 1/4 of the pipe diameter, and not less than 6 inches, each side of the pipe. Not confirmed here: Caltrans minimum cover for construction loads and plastic pipe deflection limits (Sections 64 to 66); read the section or the plans.
source: Caltrans Standard Specifications, 2025, Section 61 Drainage Facilities (read 2026-11-20; sections 64-66 not read)

title: Colorado CDOT structure backfill and compaction (Section 206)
topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
text: Colorado (CDOT 2025 Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, Section 206, Structure Excavation and Backfill). Structure backfill is Class 1 or Class 2, or Flow-Fill. Each layer of backfill is 6 inches or less. Both classes are compacted to at least 95 percent of maximum dry density, within plus or minus 2 percent of optimum moisture (soils with more than 35 percent passing the No. 200 sieve at 0 to 3 percent above optimum). Maximum density is by AASHTO T 180 for Class 1 and for A-1, A-2-4, A-2-5 and A-3 soils, and by AASHTO T 99 (as modified by CP 23) for other Class 2 materials (206.03). Flow-Fill is not compacted and goes in lifts of 3 feet or less unless the Engineer approves more; the next lift waits until the surface dents less than 3 inches with no visible water (ASTM D6024). Do not backfill against new concrete until it reaches 0.8 f'c. Bed course material is per 703.07 (206.02(b)).
source: CDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2025, Section 206 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Colorado CDOT culverts and sewers: bedding, joints, 5 percent deflection, leak test (Sections 603, 604)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Colorado (CDOT 2025 Standard Specifications, Section 603, Culverts and Sewers). Bedding: a layer of loose structure backfill at least 3 inches thick (603.05). In new embankment, build the fill to at least 0.3 times the pipe outside diameter or rise before trenching for the pipe. Storm drain joints must be watertight; sanitary sewer concrete pipe uses rubber gaskets (603.07). Deflection of metal and plastic pipe: 5 percent maximum, measured 30 days or more after installation with a mandrel, laser profile or another approved method; replaced pipe is retested after another 30 days (603.10). Reinforced concrete pipe gets a visual inspection per AASHTO LRFD Section 27.6. Sanitary sewer leak limit: no more than 0.6 gallon per inch of inside diameter per 100 feet per hour (603.09). Jacked pipe: no trenching; grout the outside with 1 part portland cement to 3 parts fine aggregate. Section 604, manholes and inlets: a manhole in pavement is not built to final grade until the paving is done; pay depth is in 5-foot steps (0 to 5.0 ft pays as 5, 5.1 to 10.0 as 10).
source: CDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2025, Sections 603 and 604 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Ten States Standards for sewers: manhole spacing, drops, alignment, steep slopes (Chapter 30)
topic: Sewer design standards: slopes, manholes, sizes
text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Chapter 30, Design of Sewers). Many state environmental agencies review sewer plans against this book or their own version of it. Manhole spacing (34.1): no more than 400 feet for sewers 15 inches and smaller, 500 feet for 18 to 30 inches, and up to 600 feet where modern cleaning equipment is available. Drop manhole (34.2): a drop pipe is needed when the incoming sewer is 24 inches or more above the manhole invert; under 24 inches the invert is filleted. Manhole size (34.3): at least 48 inches in diameter with a 24-inch minimum access opening. Alignment (33.5): sewers 24 inches and smaller are laid straight between manholes and checked by laser or lamping. Slope must be uniform between manholes (33.44). Velocities over 10 feet per second need protection against scour (33.45). Sewers on slopes of 20 percent or more are anchored: every 36 feet on 20 to 35 percent grades, 24 feet on 35 to 50 percent, 16 feet at 50 percent and steeper (33.46). Your state's own design rule and the project specs govern.
source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), GLUMRB, 2014 edition, Chapter 30 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Ten States Standards sewer tests: 100 gallon leakage limit, air test standards, 5 percent deflection, manhole test
topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition). Leakage tests (33.9): by water, leakage in or out must not exceed 100 gallons per inch of pipe diameter per mile per day, tested with at least 2 feet of positive head (33.94); by air, follow ASTM C828 for clay pipe, ASTM C924 for concrete pipe and ASTM F1417 for plastic pipe (33.95). Deflection test (33.85): required for all flexible pipe, run after the final backfill has been in place at least 30 days; no pipe may exceed 5 percent deflection; the rigid ball or mandrel is at least 95 percent of the pipe's base or average inside diameter and is pulled by hand, with no mechanical pulling devices. Manholes (34.7): inspected and tested for watertightness before going into service; air (vacuum) testing of concrete manholes follows ASTM C1244. Project specs are often tighter than these numbers, so read the testing section of your contract.
source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), GLUMRB, 2014 edition, Chapter 30 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Ten States Standards: sewer and water main separation, 10 feet and 18 inches (Section 38)
topic: Water and sewer separation distances
text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Section 38, protection of water supplies). Side by side (38.31): sewers are laid at least 10 feet horizontally from any existing or proposed water main, measured edge to edge. Where 10 feet is not practical the reviewing agency can allow closer on a case-by-case basis if the water main is in a separate trench, or on an undisturbed earth shelf at one side of the sewer trench, with the bottom of the water main at least 18 inches above the top of the sewer. If neither can be done, both lines are built of slip-on or mechanical joint pipe rated at least 150 psi and pressure tested. Crossings (38.32): at least 18 inches between the outside of the water main and the outside of the sewer, whether the water main is above or below; keep sewer joints as far as possible from water main joints. If 18 inches cannot be met, either build the sewer to water pipe standards and pressure test it, or encase the water main or the sewer in a watertight carrier pipe that extends 10 feet on both sides of the crossing. State rules vary: check the state's own separation rule.
source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), GLUMRB, 2014 edition, Chapter 30 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Montana water main rules: pressure, hydrants, sewer separation (Circular DEQ-1, Chapter 8)
topic: Spec books: water main installation, pressure test and disinfection
text: Montana (DEQ Circular DEQ-1, Standards for Water Works, 2022 edition, Chapter 8). Pressure (8.2.1): at least 35 psi normal working pressure and at least 20 psi under all flow conditions; normal working pressure should be about 60 to 80 psi. Size (8.2.2): mains serving fire hydrants are at least 6 inches; at least 3 inches where there is no fire protection. Hydrants (8.4): 6-inch lead; hydrant drains may not connect to, or be within 10 feet of, sanitary sewers or storm drains. Installation (8.7): continuous uniform bedding; enough cover to prevent freezing; pressure and leakage tests per the AWWA standards; flushing, disinfection and bacteria testing per AWWA C651. Separation from sewers (8.8): at least 10 feet horizontal, edge to edge, from gravity sanitary or storm sewers (8.8.2); at least 18 inches vertical at crossings, outside to outside (8.8.3), with reduced crossings down to 6 inches only under listed conditions such as a 150 psi tested sewer and encasement or flowable fill 10 feet each side; force mains 10 feet horizontal and 18 inches vertical (8.8.4); no water pipe through or touching a sewer manhole, and mains should be at least 10 feet from manholes (8.8.5).
source: Montana DEQ Circular DEQ-1, Standards for Water Works, 2022 edition, Chapter 8 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Ten States Standards minimum sewer slopes by pipe size (8 inch = 0.40 percent) and 2 feet per second
topic: Sewer design standards: slopes, manholes, sizes
text: Ten States Standards (Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities, 2014 edition, Section 33). A public gravity sewer carrying raw wastewater is not less than 8 inches in diameter (33.1). Sewers are designed for a mean velocity of at least 2.0 feet per second flowing full (33.41). Recommended minimum slopes, in feet per 100 feet: 8 inch 0.40; 10 inch 0.28; 12 inch 0.22; 15 inch 0.15; 18 inch 0.12; 21 inch 0.10; 24 inch 0.08 (the book's table goes on to 42 inch). Sewers 48 inches and larger are designed for at least 3.0 feet per second. Slightly flatter slopes can be allowed where the flow depth will be 0.3 of the diameter or more at design average flow (33.42). Installation (33.8): rigid pipe uses bedding Classes A, B, C or crushed stone as described in ASTM C12; flexible pipe uses embedment Classes I, II or III (ASTM D2321), carefully compacted; no debris, frozen material, large clods or stones, or organic matter in the final backfill within 2 feet of the top of the pipe (33.84). A crew does not pick the slope: lay to the plan grade, and flag it to the foreman or engineer if a plan grade is flatter than these.
source: Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), 2014 edition, Sections 33.1-33.8 (read 2026-11-20)

title: PVC sewer pipe (SDR 35, SDR 26, ASTM D3034): installation basics from the PVC Pipe Association guide
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: PVC gravity sewer pipe installation, summarized from the Uni-Bell PVC Pipe Association guide for solid-wall PVC sewer pipe (PUB-06-25). Product standard is ASTM D3034; the guide notes that since 2024 D3034 covers 3 through 60 inch, so old references to ASTM F679 for 18 inch and up are being replaced. Common stiffness classes: DR 35 and DR 26 in 4 to 15 inch; PS 46, PS 75 and PS 115 in 18 to 60 inch. Installation practice is ASTM D2321. Nothing larger than 1-1/2 inches should touch the pipe. Bedding is typically 4 to 6 inches; dig bell holes only as big as needed; bring an over-dug bottom back to grade for the full length, not just at the bells. Haunching: work material under the haunches and at least halfway up the pipe and compact it (shovel slicing works). Initial backfill: at least 6 inches over the pipe, rock free, before any machine compaction over the top. Flotation: keep the trench dry until there is about 2 pipe diameters of backfill over thin-wall pipe (DR 32.5 and higher) or 1-1/2 diameters over heavier pipe. Joints: lubricate per the maker, push until the insertion line is even with the bell lip, and do not over-insert; re-bevel and re-mark field cuts. Bending: rule of thumb radius is 200 times the pipe OD, and bending pipe over 12 inch is not recommended; do not bend and deflect the joint on the same length. Acceptance: clean, then CCTV; a go/no-go mandrel sized for 7-1/2 percent deflection per D3034 (many specs require 5 percent); low-pressure air per ASTM F1417.
source: Uni-Bell PVC Pipe Association, Installation Guide for Solid-Wall PVC Sewer Pipe, PUB-06-25 (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Ductile iron pipe joints: mechanical joint bolt torque and maximum joint deflection (DIPRA guide)
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: Ductile iron pipe joints, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe (revised May 2015). Mechanical joint bolt torque (Table 4): 5/8 inch bolts on 3 inch joints 45 to 60 ft-lb; 3/4 inch bolts on 4 to 24 inch 75 to 90 ft-lb; 1 inch bolts on 30 to 36 inch 100 to 120 ft-lb; 1-1/4 inch bolts on 42 to 48 inch 120 to 150 ft-lb. Tighten in a star pattern and go around again until every bolt is in range. Push-on joints: clean the bell groove and the spigot, seat the gasket, lubricate the gasket and the plain end (not the socket), bevel field cuts, push straight home and deflect only after the joint is made. Maximum push-on deflection on an 18-foot length (Table 5): 5 degrees, about 19 inches of offset, for 3 to 12 inch; 3 degrees, about 11 inches, for 14 to 42 inch. Mechanical joints (Table 6): 6 inch 7 degrees (27 inches); 8 to 12 inch 5 degrees (20 inches); 14 inch 3.5 degrees; 24 inch about 2 degrees. Cutting: abrasive saw (about a minute per inch of diameter), then grind and bevel the end. Check the pipe maker's own table for the exact joint: restrained joints allow less.
source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Ductile iron pipe: laying conditions Types 1 to 5, cover, trench width, polywrap (DIPRA guide)
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: Ductile iron pipe laying, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe (revised May 2015). Laying conditions (the trench types used in AWWA C150 and C600): Type 1 flat-bottom trench with loose backfill (not for 14 inch and larger); Type 2 flat-bottom trench, backfill lightly consolidated to the pipe centerline; Type 3 pipe bedded in at least 4 inches of loose soil, backfill lightly consolidated to the top of the pipe; Type 4 bedding of sand, gravel or crushed stone to 1/8 of the pipe diameter (4 inch minimum), backfill compacted to about 80 percent Standard Proctor; Type 5 bedded to the centerline in compacted granular material (4 inch minimum under the pipe), backfill compacted to about 90 percent Standard Proctor. The plans say which type. Cover is generally 2.5 to 3 feet minimum, deeper in frost country. Keep rock at least 6 inches away from pipe 24 inch and smaller and 9 inches from 30 inch and larger. Polyethylene encasement (AWWA C105) in corrosive soil: one tube per pipe length, overlapped about 1 foot at joints, taped at the ends and about every 2 feet, with slack at the joints; repair tears with tape. Before tapping polywrapped pipe, wrap 2 to 3 layers of tape around the pipe at the tap. Direct taps: 3/4 inch on all sizes, 1 inch on 6 inch and larger; bigger services need a saddle or tapping sleeve per the guide's table.
source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Water main pressure test, flushing and chlorination basics (DIPRA guide, AWWA C600 and C651)
topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
text: Testing a new ductile iron water main, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide (revised May 2015), which follows AWWA C600 and C651. Pressure test: at least 1.5 times the working pressure at the lowest point of the section, held for at least 2 hours (150 psi working means a 225 psi test). Measure the make-up water needed to hold pressure; examples of the testing allowance at 150 psi are about 0.50 gallon per hour per 1,000 feet of 6 inch and 0.99 for 12 inch. Brace or restrain temporary plugs and caps. Flush at 3.0 feet per second: roughly 400 gpm for a 6 inch main and 1,060 gpm for a 12 inch. Chlorination (AWWA C651): tablet method, granules at the start and every 500 feet and 5-gram tablets at joints, fill slowly at 1 foot per second or less, hold 24 hours (48 hours if the water is colder than 41 F), about 25 mg/L; continuous feed, at least 25 mg/L going in and at least 10 mg/L left after 24 hours; slug method, at least 100 mg/L for at least 3 hours, start over if it drops below 50 mg/L. Flush the strong chlorine out within about a day, dechlorinate where the discharge rule requires it, then take bacteria samples. The water agency's spec governs.
source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Thrust at bends and dead ends: example forces and soil bearing values (DIPRA guide)
topic: Thrust blocks and restrained joints
text: Thrust restraint basics, summarized from the DIPRA Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe (revised May 2015). Water pressure pushes on every bend, tee, reducer, valve and dead end. Example thrust at 100 psi: a 12 inch 90 degree bend pushes about 19,353 lb and a 12 inch dead end about 13,685 lb; thrust scales straight with pressure, so use test pressure, not working pressure. Example soil bearing values at 4 feet deep (Table 8): muck 0, sand about 4,000 lb per square foot, hard clay about 9,000. Common practice is block bearing area = thrust divided by the allowable soil bearing, poured against undisturbed soil. Blocks are concrete of at least 2,000 psi, cured at least five days before testing. Mechanical joints by themselves hold no thrust. Restrained joints (or wedge-action glands) are used instead of blocks where space is tight or the soil behind the block may be dug out later; the restrained length comes from the engineer or the agency table. Always build what the plans or the agency thrust block detail shows; these numbers are examples, not a design.
source: Ductile Iron Pipe Research Association (DIPRA), Installation Guide for Ductile Iron Pipe, revised May 2015, hosted by McWane (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: ADS N-12 corrugated HDPE pipe: minimum and maximum cover (TN 2.01)
topic: Pipe cover: minimum and maximum burial depth
text: Corrugated HDPE storm pipe cover, summarized from ADS Technical Note TN 2.01 (rev. AB, 2024) for N-12 pipe. Minimum cover under H-20, H-25 or HL-93 traffic: 1 foot over the crown for 4 to 48 inch pipe and 2 feet for 54 and 60 inch; flexible pavement thickness does not count toward it, and construction or paving equipment may need more temporary cover (see the ADS Drainage Handbook installation section). Maximum cover depends on the backfill around the pipe. Examples in feet for 12 / 24 / 36 / 48 / 60 inch: Class 1 compacted stone 35 / 28 / 26 / 25 / 25; Class 2 at 95 percent 24 / 20 / 18 / 17 / 17; Class 2 at 90 percent 17 / 13 / 12 / 11 / 11; Class 2 at 85 percent 8 / 7 / 7 / 7 / 6; Class 3 at 95 percent 17 / 14 / 13 / 12 / 12; Class 3 at 90 percent 11 / 10 / 9 / 7 / 7. The table assumes installation per ASTM D2321, no groundwater pressure and 120 pcf soil. These are general guidance, not a project design, and other makers' pipe has its own tables.
source: ADS (Advanced Drainage Systems) Technical Note TN 2.01, Minimum and Maximum Burial Depth for Corrugated HDPE Pipe (per AASHTO), rev. AB, copyright 2024 (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Concrete pipe (RCP) Standard Installations Types 1 to 4: bedding thickness and compaction (ACPA, ASTM C1479)
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: Reinforced concrete pipe installation, summarized from the American Concrete Pipe Association installation manual. The four Standard Installations (Type 1 best, Type 4 least effort) are the same ones in ASTM C1479 and ASCE 15, and the plans say which type the pipe class was designed for. Bedding thickness under the pipe: outside diameter divided by 24, not less than 3 inches; on rock, outside diameter divided by 12, not less than 6 inches. Leave the middle bedding under the pipe loose so the pipe seats. Soil categories: I clean gravelly sand, II sandy silt, III silty clay. Haunch and outer bedding compaction (Standard Proctor): Type 1, 95 percent Category I; Type 2, 90 percent Category I or 95 percent Category II; Type 3, 85 percent Category I, 90 percent II or 95 percent III; Type 4, none needed except 85 percent if Category III soil is used. Lower side: Type 1, 90 percent I, 95 percent II or 100 percent III; Types 2 and 3, 85 percent I, 90 percent II or 95 percent III. Trench width guide: 1.25 times the pipe outside diameter plus 1 foot. Lay from the outlet end with bells upstream; clean and lubricate bell, spigot and gasket; bar and block works up to about 24 inch, larger pipe needs a puller. Put at least 3 feet of compacted backfill over pipe or box before equipment crosses unless it was designed for that load.
source: American Concrete Pipe Association, Concrete Pipe and Box Culvert Installation manual (our summary; read 2026-11-20). Standard Installations are the ones in ASTM C1479 and ASCE 15.

title: Concrete pipe acceptance tests: infiltration, exfiltration, air, joint and vacuum tests (ACPA)
topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
text: Testing concrete sewer and storm pipe, summarized from the American Concrete Pipe Association installation manual. Infiltration test: only meaningful when groundwater is at least 2 feet over the crown; the manual's base allowance is 200 gallons per inch of diameter per mile per day at 6 feet of head, rising to 282 at 12 feet. Exfiltration test: base head 3 feet; single reaches can run over if the project average passes. Low-pressure air test follows ASTM C924 and is limited to pipe 24 inch and smaller; it finds construction defects but does not measure water leakage. Larger pipe is tested one joint at a time with air or water under ASTM C1103. Vacuum testing: ASTM C1214 for pipe 4 to 36 inch, ASTM C1244 for manholes. Visual inspection looks for debris, cracks, joints fully home and sealed, smooth inverts and properly set frames. The project spec sets the pass numbers; many agencies allow far less leakage than 200 gallons (the Ten States figure is 100).
source: American Concrete Pipe Association, Concrete Pipe and Box Culvert Installation manual (our summary; read 2026-11-20). Standard Installations are the ones in ASTM C1479 and ASCE 15.

title: C900 PVC water pipe installation (AWWA C605): trench, cover, joints, bending, testing rules
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: C900 PVC pressure pipe installation, summarized from Westlake Pipe's 2025 installation guides, which follow AWWA C605 (the PVC pressure pipe installation standard) and AWWA manual M23. Trench: clear width at the pipe springline at least 18 inches or pipe OD plus 1 foot, whichever is greater; no more than pipe diameter plus 2 feet at the crown; 4 inches of soil cushion where there is rock. Embedment: work material under the haunches, particle size 3/4 inch or smaller, at least 1 foot of initial backfill over the crown, compacted to what the engineer specifies. Cover: 24 inches under heavy traffic (ASTM D2774). Flotation: about 1.5 pipe diameters of cover. Joints: clean, check the gasket, lubricate the spigot bevel and the gasket with potable-safe lubricant, keep the lengths straight and push to the insertion line without over-inserting. Joint deflection for this pipe is only 1 degree (about 4-3/16 inches of offset on a 20-foot length). Bending the barrel instead is allowed by hand in 12 inch and smaller: minimum radius about 100 feet for 4 inch, 144 feet for 6 inch, 189 feet for 8 inch, 231 feet for 10 inch, 275 feet for 12 inch; never bend and deflect the same length. PVC grows or shrinks about 0.36 inch per 100 feet for each 10 F. Field cuts: square, bevel, re-mark the insertion line. No direct taps on C909 PVCO pipe. Testing: water only, never air; fill at 1 foot per second or less and vent high points; never test above the pipe's pressure rating; disinfect per AWWA C651. Up to two years of outdoor sun exposure is acceptable. Other makers' limits differ, so use the guide for the pipe on the truck.
source: Westlake Pipe & Fittings, Installation Guide for C900 PVC and C909 PVCO pressure pipe, MU-IG-013-US-EN-1025.1, 2025; and Municipal Installation Guide MU-IG-017, 2025 (our summary; read 2026-11-20). Both follow AWWA C605.

title: JM Eagle solvent-weld PVC pipe and conduit: trench, cover, cement set times (JME-07B)
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: Solvent-weld PVC pressure pipe and PVC electrical conduit, summarized from JM Eagle's installation guide JME-07B (revised March 2011). Bedding 4 to 6 inches compacted, with bell holes; on rock, a cushion of at least 4 inches of sand or select backfill (6 inches in rock cuts). Haunching and initial backfill by hand, no rocks over 1.5 inches, tamped in layers of 6 inches or less, to at least 1 foot above the pipe; 90 percent density under pavement. Trench width: pipe OD plus 1 foot minimum at the springline, pipe OD plus 2 feet maximum at the top of the pipe. Cover: 12 inches where frost is not a concern, otherwise 6 inches below the deepest recorded frost. No rolling equipment until 18 inches of backfill is over the pipe; hydro-hammers need at least 3 feet. Solvent joints: dry fit (pipe should go 1/3 to 3/4 of the way into the socket), prime, cement both parts, push home with a quarter turn, look for a full bead. Minimum set time before handling: 30 minutes at 60 to 100 F, 1 hour at 40 to 60 F, 2 hours at 20 to 40 F, 4 hours at 0 to 20 F. No deflection at solvent joints: make curves by bending the pipe; snake small pipe in the trench. Pressure test is generally 25 percent above normal operating pressure and never above the pipe's rating. Never use compressed air or gas in PVC pressure pipe. JM Eagle's gravity sewer guide is JME-05B.
source: JM Eagle (J-M Manufacturing), Solvent Weld and Electrical Conduit Installation Guide, JME-07B, revised March 2011 (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Corrugated metal pipe (CMP) installation: bedding, 8-inch lifts, 90 percent, balanced backfill, cover (Contech)
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: Corrugated metal pipe installation, summarized from Contech's CMP Installation Guide (June 2023). Bedding: 4 to 6 inches of well-graded granular material on a firm foundation; dig out soft spots and replace with granular fill. Backfill: angular, well-graded granular soil (AASHTO A-1, A-2 or A-3), nothing over 3 inches, placed in loose lifts of about 8 inches and compacted to 90 percent of AASHTO T99 (95 percent in the haunches of pipe-arch). Work material into the haunches with a shovel or rod. Keep the two sides balanced: never let one side get more than 24 inches higher than the other, including between barrels. Use flowable fill (CLSM) in thin lifts where barrels are too close to compact, letting each lift set so the pipe does not float. Minimum cover for highway loads is span divided by 8 (not less than 12 inches in common practice), in place and compacted before traffic. Light tracked equipment such as a small dozer needs at least 12 inches of compacted cover; heavy construction equipment needs more per the guide's tables. Lay from the downstream end and build the outlet first so rain can drain. Unload with forks or non-metallic slings; never dump pipe off the truck or lift bundles by the strapping.
source: Contech Engineered Solutions, CMP Installation Guide, June 2023 (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Clay pipe (VCP) bedding classes and load factors, ASTM C12
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: Vitrified clay pipe is installed under ASTM C12. Clay is rigid pipe, so the bedding class sets how much load the pipe can carry: the pipe's bearing strength is multiplied by the bedding load factor. Load factors published by the National Clay Pipe Institute from ASTM C12: Class D (flat trench bottom, least support) 1.1; Class C 1.5; Class B 1.9; crushed stone encasement 2.2; controlled low-strength material (CLSM, flowable fill) 2.8; concrete cradle 3.4. The plans call out the class; a crew that builds Class C where Class B was designed has cut the pipe's safe load by about a fifth. Shape bell holes so the barrel, not the bell, carries the load, and haunch the pipe by shovel slicing. Ten States Standards (33.83) point to these same ASTM C12 classes for rigid sewer pipe.
source: National Clay Pipe Institute bedding sheet (2021), load factors from ASTM C12, Standard Practice for Installing Vitrified Clay Pipe Lines (our summary; read 2026-11-20)

title: Georgia GDOT storm drain pipe: video and laser inspection, 5 and 7.5 percent deflection (Section 550)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Georgia (GDOT Section 550, Storm Drain Pipe, Pipe-Arch Culverts, and Side Drain Pipe, supplemental specification revised 2015). Foundation and backfill follow Section 207 and Georgia Standards 1030D and 1030P. Thermoplastic pipe outside the roadbed in fills up to 10 feet uses Class II B2 or better soil for HDPE and Class II B3 or better for PVC and polypropylene; above 10 feet, graded aggregate (550.3.03). Thermoplastic joints are at least silt tight (550.3.05.C). Post-installation inspection (550.3.06): once compacted backfill reaches 8 feet or final cover is complete, with at least seven days notice to the Engineer; low-distortion video with laser profiling of 100 percent of storm drain pipe and at least 10 percent of side drain pipe on state route projects, by NASSCO PACP certified operators; manual inspection is allowed in pipe over 48 inches. Deflection over 5 percent of nominal diameter needs an evaluation by a Professional Engineer; over 7.5 percent is remediated or replaced. Joint separation over 1 inch must be fixed. Lift thickness and compaction percent are not confirmed here (they are not in Section 550); see Section 207.
source: Georgia DOT Supplemental Specification Section 550, Storm Drain Pipe, Pipe-Arch Culverts, and Side Drain Pipe (revised 2015; read 2026-11-20)

title: Kentucky KYTC culvert and storm sewer pipe: bedding, 6-inch lifts, 95 percent, 48 inches cover (Section 701)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Kentucky (KYTC Standard Specifications, Section 701, culvert pipe, entrance pipe and storm sewer pipe). Bedding: No. 8 or No. 9-M stone or fine aggregate; do not use DGA or gravel base (701.02.04). Backfill in 6-inch lifts compacted to not less than 95 percent of maximum density by Kentucky Method KM 64-511 (701.03.06). Keep construction equipment and traffic off the pipe until there is 48 inches of cover over it (701.03.07). Joints are soil tight and wrapped with geotextile; concrete pipe joints may be mortar (1 cement to 2 sand), asphalt mastic, rubber gaskets or butyl sealant, with tied joints within 12 feet of the outlet on slopes 3:1 or steeper; metal pipe bands are at least 12 inches wide for pipe 54 inches and smaller; thermoplastic pipe uses bell and spigot with elastomeric seals (701.03.05). Trench limits are on the Standard Drawings.
source: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, Division 700, Sections 701, 705, 706, as posted by KYTC (edition year not shown in the file; read 2026-11-20)

title: Kentucky KYTC pipeline camera inspection, mandrel and deflection pay cuts (Section 705); boring and jacking (706)
topic: Spec books: pipe testing and inspection (air, water, mandrel, video)
text: Kentucky (KYTC Standard Specifications, Section 705, pipeline inspection). Installed pipe gets a camera inspection under Kentucky Method KM 64-114, with at least 24 hours notice to the Engineer, 30 days or more after earthwork is complete to within 1 foot of finished subgrade (705.02). Flexible pipe up to 48 inches can be checked with a mandrel that has at least 9 legs (705.03). Deflection table (705.05): 0 to 5.0 percent, full payment; 5.1 to 9.9 percent, 50 percent payment; 10 percent or greater, remove and replace. Section 706, boring and jacking: access pits on both sides, guide rails kept to line and grade, casing fitted tight to the bore with continuous welds. Minimum steel casing wall: 0.375 inch for 18 inch and smaller, 0.500 inch for 24 to 30 inch, 0.532 inch for 36 inch, 0.625 inch for 42 inch (706.02.01).
source: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, Division 700, Sections 701, 705, 706, as posted by KYTC (edition year not shown in the file; read 2026-11-20)

title: Iowa DOT corrugated metal and plastic culverts: cover and the 5 percent deflection test (Section 2417)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Iowa (Iowa DOT Standard Specifications, Section 2417, Corrugated Culverts, online version revised 10/20/2026). Corrugated metal or polyethylene roadway culverts get Class B bedding as shown in the contract documents (2417.03.C.1). Minimum cover: 1 foot over entrance culverts and 2 feet over roadway culverts; if construction traffic will cross, roadway culvert cover goes up to the pipe's nominal diameter or 3 feet, whichever is greater (2417.03.B). Polyethylene pipe deflection test (2417.03.C.2): at least 10 percent of locations, no sooner than 30 calendar days after backfill and before paving; the inside diameter may not shrink more than 5.0 percent; pipe 30 inches and smaller is tested with a nine-point mandrel, larger pipe is checked along its whole length. City street and utility work in Iowa usually follows SUDAS instead of the DOT book.
source: Iowa DOT Standard Specifications (current online General Supplemental series, page revised 10/20/2026), Section 2417 Corrugated Culverts (read 2026-11-20)

title: Montana MDT culverts, storm drains and sewers: 6-inch lifts and 4 feet of cover before heavy equipment (Section 603)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Montana (MDT Standard Specifications, 2025 book, Section 603, Culverts, Storm Drains, Sanitary Sewers). Bedding is placed per Section 207 and the Detailed Drawings, with material tamped firmly under the pipe haunches (603.03.2, 603.04.3(B)). Backfill goes in layers of 6 inches loose thickness or less, to the moisture and density required by Subsection 203.03.3 (the percent is set there, not in 603). Heavy equipment stays off until cover is at least 4 feet or one-half the pipe diameter, whichever is greater (603.03.4(A)). Round concrete pipe joints are watertight with rubber gaskets (603.03.3(A)); siphon and irrigation pipe get a water-tightness test (MT 420); manhole connections follow ASTM C923. Section 604, manholes and inlets: backfill in loose layers of 6 inches or less, foundation compacted for full bearing.
source: Montana DOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2025 redline book, Sections 603 and 604 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Wyoming WYDOT culvert excavation and backfill: 8-inch lifts at 95 percent (Section 206)
topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
text: Wyoming (WYDOT 2021 Standard Specifications, Section 206, Excavation and Backfill for Culverts). Backfill in loose layers of about 8 inches, each compacted to at least 95.0 percent of maximum density at moisture between plus 2 and minus 4 percent of optimum (206.4.5.1). Compact the last 6 inches below structures or bedding to at least 95.0 percent (206.4.4). Over water and sewer lines, hand-place the first 12 inches. Do not backfill against cast-in-place boxes until 14 calendar days or 80 percent of design strength. Flowable fill: at least 12 inches over the conduit and no vehicle loads until 24 hours after it sets (206.4.5.3). Pipe bedding and laying are in Section 603 (603.4.4 and 603.4.5). Section 212, structure backfill: loose layers of about 8 inches compacted to the density of the adjacent material, placed evenly on both sides.
source: Wyoming DOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2021 edition, Sections 206 and 212 (read 2026-11-20; Section 603 not read)

title: Arizona ADOT pipe culverts and storm drains (Section 501) and the 2027 spec book change
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Arizona (ADOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction). Edition: the 2021 edition is in use now; ADOT says the 2027 edition applies to all projects advertising on and after January 4, 2027, electronic only, so check which book your contract names. Section 501, Pipe Culvert and Storm Drains, as described in ADOT's own Construction Manual (March 2025): a written trenching plan is required for trenches deeper than 5 feet (501-1); trench widths and the minimum 1 foot of cover are on Standard Drawing C-13.15, and cover must be increased for construction traffic, which is the contractor's responsibility (501-3.01); pipe 36 inches and larger in a trench is bedded in cement-treated slurry from the trench bottom to the springline (501-3.04); replacement backfill is compacted to 95 percent of maximum density (501-3.07(B)). The manual advises inspectors that heavy vibratory equipment should not run directly over pipe until there is at least 3 feet of cover and that nothing should be placed on flowable fill for 24 hours. In the Phoenix area, city and county work usually follows the MAG Uniform Standard Specifications instead.
source: ADOT Construction Manual, Chapter 5, Sections 501-505 (March 2025), describing the ADOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction; edition notice at azdot.gov/business/contracts-and-specifications (both read 2026-11-20)

title: Texas, Fort Worth utility trench spec: embedment, 12-inch lifts, 95 and 98 percent, test frequency (33 05 10)
topic: Spec books: trench, bedding, backfill and compaction
text: Texas, City of Fort Worth (Standard Specification 33 05 10, Utility Trench Excavation, Embedment and Backfill, revised April 2, 2021). Embedment and initial backfill go 6 to 12 inches above the pipe for water lines and for sanitary sewer and HDPE storm pipe; reinforced concrete storm pipe is embedded to the spring line; polypropylene storm pipe gets crushed rock to the top of pipe (3.4.D). Embedment and initial backfill are compacted to 95 percent Standard Proctor (ASTM D698). Final backfill: loose lifts of 12 inches or less; 95 percent under existing or future pavement less than 15 feet deep, 98 percent for select fill 15 feet and deeper, 95 percent outside pavement; moisture from minus 2 to plus 5 percent of optimum (3.4.E.3). Density tests: at least one per 2 vertical feet of compacted backfill and at least every 200 feet of trench, staggered by lift (3.7.A.2.d). Water lines 12 inch and smaller: top of pipe at least 42 inches below proposed grade unless the drawings say otherwise. Trench safety follows OSHA Subpart P and an Excavation Safety Plan designed by a Texas-licensed engineer. Other cities in the area use the NCTCOG specifications.
source: City of Fort Worth Standard Specification 33 05 10, Utility Trench Excavation, Embedment and Backfill, revised April 2, 2021 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Texas water and sewer separation: the 9-foot rule (TCEQ 30 TAC 217.53 and 290.44)
topic: Water and sewer separation distances
text: Texas uses 9 feet, not 10. TCEQ rules: sewer pipe and manholes should be at least 9 feet from water lines, in a separate trench and below the water line where possible (30 TAC 217.53(d); 30 TAC 290.44(e)(1)). When 9 feet cannot be met, parallel lines: the water line at least 2 feet above and 4 feet to the side of the sewer, with 150 psi pressure-rated sewer pipe, or encasement (217.53(d)(6); 290.44(e)(4)(A)). Sewer crossing under a water line: 150 psi pipe with at least 6 inches of separation, one length at least 18 feet long centered on the water line; or other pipe with at least 2 feet of separation and cement-stabilized sand; or a casing pipe at least two sizes larger with spacers no more than 5 feet apart (217.53(d)(7)). A manhole within 9 feet of a water line must pass the leak test or get at least 1 foot of cement-stabilized sand. Water lines: at least 24 inches of cover, 35 psi minimum pressure, fire hydrants not within 9 feet of sewer lines, new mains disinfected per AWWA C651 with at least one bacteria sample per 1,000 feet (290.44).
source: 30 Texas Administrative Code 217.53 (TCEQ, wastewater collection pipe design; amended eff. 12/4/2015) and 30 TAC 290.44 (water distribution), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-11-20

title: Florida water main separation from sewer, storm and reclaimed lines (Rule 62-555.314)
topic: Water and sewer separation distances
text: Florida has its own separation numbers (F.A.C. Rule 62-555.314, amended effective 2/26/2025). Side by side, a new or relocated water main is at least: 3 feet from storm sewers, stormwater force mains and regulated reclaimed water lines; 3 feet, preferably 10, from vacuum sanitary sewers; 6 feet, preferably 10, from gravity or pressure sanitary sewers and wastewater force mains (gravity sewer can come down to 3 feet if the bottom of the water main is at least 6 inches above the top of the sewer); 10 feet from onsite sewage (septic) systems. Crossing a gravity or vacuum sewer or storm sewer: water main at least 6 inches, preferably 12, above, or at least 12 inches below; above is preferred. Crossing a pressure sewer, force main or reclaimed line: at least 12 inches above or below. At crossings, center one full length of water main, or keep water main joints at least 3 feet from storm and vacuum sewer joints and 6 feet from sanitary sewer and force main joints. No water main may pass through or touch a sanitary sewer manhole. The Department can allow exceptions with extra protection such as pressure-rated sewer pipe, a casing or concrete encasement.
source: Florida Administrative Code Rule 62-555.314, Location of Public Water System Mains (amended eff. 2/26/2025), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-11-20

title: Florida FDOT Standard Specifications: which edition is in force (July-to-June books)
topic: Spec books: which edition applies
text: Florida (FDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction). FDOT publishes a new eBook each fiscal year: the FY 2026-27 book took effect July 1, 2026 and the FY 2027-28 book takes effect July 1, 2027; your contract names the one that applies. The sections a pipe crew lives in are Section 125 (Excavation for Structures and Pipe), Section 430 (Pipe Culverts) and Section 425 (Inlets, Manholes, and Junction Boxes), with jack and bore in Section 556. The numbers in those sections are not confirmed in this library (the files would not open here), so for lift thickness, density and pipe inspection go to the book itself at fdot.gov/specifications. County and city utility work in Florida usually follows the utility's own standards, and water main separation follows state Rule 62-555.314.
source: FDOT Standard Specification Library, fdot.gov/specifications/standard-specification-library (edition list read 2026-11-20); section numbers not re-read

title: Indiana INDOT pipe: mandrel testing of plastic pipe, Section 715
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Indiana (INDOT Standard Specifications Section 715, Pipe Culverts, and Storm and Sanitary Sewers, as changed by Recurring Special Provision 715-R-809 dated 09-01-26). After the visual or video inspection, plastic pipe is mandrel tested: corrugated and smooth-wall polyethylene, corrugated polypropylene, and profile and smooth-wall PVC. The Engineer picks the runs, and at least 10 percent of the total length of each material is tested; underdrain pipe is exempt. Backfill for corrugated pipe may not have particles larger than half the corrugation depth. Thermoplastic and metal pipe must come from INDOT's qualified products list. The deflection limit, lift thickness and compaction numbers are in the base Section 715 and Section 211 text, which was not read here, so those numbers are not confirmed.
source: INDOT Recurring Special Provision 715-R-809, Pipe Culverts, and Storm and Sanitary Sewers, dated 09-01-26 (read 2026-11-20)

title: North Dakota NDDOT culverts and storm drains: 6-inch lifts, 90 percent, 95 percent mandrel (Section 714)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: North Dakota (NDDOT 2023 Standard Specifications, Section 714, Culverts, Storm Drains, Edgedrains, and Underdrains). Bedding is tamped under both haunches up to 15 percent of the pipe height with hand-held air tampers (714.04 A.4). Backfill in lifts of 6 inches or less; aggregate backfill compacted to at least 90 percent of maximum dry density at 2 points below to 3 points above optimum moisture (714.04 A.10 and A.11). Cover before equipment crosses: the book gives no number and sends you to the pipe maker's recommendation (714.04 A.12). Deflection test: metal and thermoplastic pipe under mainline and paved crossroads is tested at least 30 days after installation with a nine-point mandrel at least 95 percent of the inside diameter; pipe the mandrel will not pass is replaced (714.04 A.8). Concrete pipe joints are wrapped in geotextile. Jacked steel pipe: bore without water, start within 0.1 foot of staked grade, and stay within 1/2 foot of line and grade (714.04 C). Manholes and inlets (722): backfill lifts of 6 inches or less at 90 percent. Water and sewer lines (724): bedding up the sides to one-third of the pipe diameter, backfill in 6-inch loose lifts.
source: North Dakota DOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction, 2023, Sections 714, 722, 724 (read 2026-11-20)

title: Ohio ODOT pipe culverts and sewers: installation plan, 7.5 percent deflection, 30 to 90 day inspection (Item 611)
topic: Spec books: culvert and storm drain pipe installation
text: Ohio (ODOT Construction and Material Specifications, Item 611, Pipe Culverts, Sewers, Drains, and Drainage Structures). These numbers are from the 2013 online edition; the current 2023 book was not checked, so treat them as not confirmed for a current job and read Item 611 in the contract's edition. In Item 611 the contractor's installation plan sets trench dimensions, bedding, lift thickness and compaction (611.04, 611.06); rock or unsuitable material is removed at least 6 inches below the pipe and replaced with structural backfill; if no bedding is used, the middle third of the bed is loosened. With low-strength mortar bedding, the mortar backfill is carried at least 6 inches over the conduit. Performance inspection (611.12): for runs over 20 feet, 30 to 90 days after finished grade, with 5 workdays notice to the Engineer and a video record. Metal and plastic conduit is repaired or replaced if the mandrel will not pass or the laser profile shows more than 7.5 percent deflection (611.13). Sanitary concrete pipe joints are tested under ASTM C969 or C1103. Structure inverts must be within 0.1 foot or 5 percent of the pipe diameter, whichever is greater (611.14).
source: Ohio DOT Construction and Material Specifications, Item 611, 2013 online edition (read 2026-11-20). The current book is the 2023 C&MS with yearly updates, which was not read.

title: Nevada NDOT Standard Specifications: current edition and where pipe work is covered
topic: Spec books: which edition applies
text: Nevada (NDOT Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction). NDOT lists the 2024 edition as current. The numbers for pipe culverts, structure excavation and backfill in the 2024 book are not confirmed in this library because the file would not open; get them from the book on NDOT's Standard Specifications and Plans page or from the NDOT Specifications office. In the Las Vegas valley, city, county and water district work normally follows the Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings for Clark County instead, and in the Reno area the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (the Orange Book), each with the agency's own amendments. Your contract says which book governs.
source: Nevada DOT, Standard Specifications, Standard Plans, and Design Guides page (edition list read 2026-11-20; the 2024 book itself would not open)

title: Utah UDOT Standard Specifications: editions listed and where city work differs
topic: Spec books: which edition applies
text: Utah (UDOT Standard Specifications). UDOT's standards page lists yearly books, with 2027 the newest listed above 2026 and 2025; the contract names the one that applies. The numbers in UDOT's drainage pipe and backfill sections are not confirmed in this library because the files would not open; read the section in the contract's edition on UDOT's standards page or ask the UDOT Standards Coordinator. City, county and district utility work along the Wasatch Front usually follows the APWA Utah Chapter Manual of Standard Specifications and Plans with local amendments, not the UDOT book.
source: UDOT Standard Specifications and Standard Drawings page (edition list read 2026-11-20; the books are in an online folder that would not open)

title: Oregon ODOT 2024 book: effective date, video speed, boring and jacking, adjusting manholes
topic: Spec books: jacking, boring and tunneling
text: Oregon (2024 Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction). This edition applies to ODOT projects bid on or after Dec. 1, 2023, and many cities use it with their own special provisions. Trench width at the surface is as narrow as practical but not less than 24 inches (00405.41(c)); the pipe zone runs to at least 8 inches over the pipe (00405.02); trench backfill is 95 percent of AASHTO T 99 under roadway and shoulders and 90 percent elsewhere (00405.46(c)(2)). Video inspection: the camera moves no faster than 30 feet per minute while recording (00445.74). Deflection mandrel: at least 9 vanes, 95 percent of the pipe's initial inside diameter, not less than 30 days after backfill (00445.73(c)). Tunneling, boring and jacking (Section 00406): pipe, casing or sleeves are jacked or bored to the required line and grade, and jacked casings 36 inches and larger get grout nipples at 10-foot centers when pressure grouting is specified (00406.12). Manhole vacuum test: 10 inches of mercury, timed to 9 inches (00470.71(b)). Adjusting structures (00490.46): no more than 24 inches from the new frame grade to the top of the cone.
source: Oregon Standard Specifications for Construction, 2024 (ODOT/APWA Oregon Chapter), Sections 00405, 00406, 00445, 00470, 00490 (read 2026-11-20)

title: PVC gravity sewer pipe (SDR 35): cover before traffic, joint deflection and bending limits (Westlake guide)
topic: Pipe installation guides by material
text: PVC gravity sewer pipe (ASTM D3034), summarized from Westlake Pipe's 2024 installation guide. Embedment follows ASTM D2321 Classes I to IV. Cover before traffic crosses: 24 inches or one pipe diameter, whichever is larger, with Class I (crushed rock) embedment; 36 inches or one pipe diameter with Classes II to IV; 48 inches before a hydrohammer is used over the pipe. Flotation: about 1.5 pipe diameters of cover for SDR 32.5 and heavier pipe. Deflection: the guide uses 7.5 percent maximum at 30 days (ASTM D3034 appendix), checked with a go/no-go mandrel after 30 days; many agencies specify 5 percent. Joints: clean, lubricate the spigot bevel and gasket, keep the lengths straight, push with bar and block until the bell edge is on the insertion line, and do not over-insert. Joint deflection for this pipe is 1 degree: about 2.9 inches of offset on a 14-foot length and 4.2 inches on a 20-foot length. Bending the barrel by hand instead: minimum radius about 35 feet for 4 inch, 52 feet for 6 inch, 70 feet for 8 inch, 85 feet for 10 inch, 104 feet for 12 inch and 128 feet for 15 inch; not recommended above 15 inch; never bend and deflect the same length. Low-pressure air testing follows ASTM F1417. Laying lengths are 14 and 20 feet.
source: Westlake Pipe & Fittings, ASTM D3034 PVC Gravity Sewer Pipe Installation Guide, MU-IG-003-US-EN-0724.1, 2024 (our summary; read 2026-11-20)
